findings.description: AWS access key and secret key are embedded in plaintext in the instance user_data script, which is visible to anyone with DescribeInstanceAttribute permissions and is stored unencrypted in the Terraform state and EC2 metadata.
The instance does not set metadata_options to require IMDSv2 (http_tokens = required), leaving the legacy instance metadata service enabled and vulnerable to SSRF-based credential theft.
The EBS volume does not enable encryption (the encrypted attribute is commented out), so data at rest on this volume is stored unprotected.
The snapshot is created from an unencrypted source volume and inherits the lack of encryption, exposing data at rest and any future volumes restored from it.
The security group allows inbound TCP port 22 (SSH) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the management interface of the instance to the entire internet.
The security group allows all outbound traffic (protocol -1) to 0.0.0.0/0, permitting unrestricted data exfiltration or command-and-control communication from a compromised instance.

map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, causing instances launched in this subnet to automatically receive public IP addresses and be directly reachable from the internet, contrary to layered network isolation.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, causing instances launched in this subnet to automatically receive public IP addresses, expanding the internet-facing attack surface.

The S3 bucket storing VPC flow logs has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so sensitive network traffic metadata is stored unencrypted, and force_destroy is enabled without any access controls restricting who can read the logs.
